posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
Looking at the description again, this game sounds like it will put some cool twists on the XCOM style. The stances and support actions will really add to the feel of a hero team leaning on each other to ultimately defeat the villain. I love the description of a bank heist foiling turning into…presumably, Baron Blade showing up. It would be cool to have a base in Freedom Plaza, assigning squads of heroes to deal with minor events throughout the city but not knowing if a supervillain might turn up.

The stances sound particularly interesting in light of the two heroes down. Bunker has obvious applications: his modes. So does Wraith: stealth combat, melee combat, and probably something investigation-related. It’s not obvious to me how to apply that kind of scheme to every hero we know, though.

Something else intriguing: the Sentinels of Freedom teaser site starts with the sentence: “Prepare for a story driven campaign within the Sentinel Comics universe.” Do you think this means it actually takes place in what we previously knew as the RPG timeline? That makes sense for a game where you can build your own heroes, and I’m excited that there might be a way I can get at the RPG lore and fun as a guy who doesn’t enjoy role playing very much.

posts.cooked: It doesn't sound like they're helping very much, though.  Adam is directing the art, not creating it.  I think that just means he's made some sample artwork (already done), and Underbite's artist(s) will match it and run it by Adam for his approval.  Christopher is responsible for "story," which could be anything from writing an outline, which would take him less than an hour, to writing every line of dialogue, which would take days if not weeks.  I'm guessing something closer to the former, since he knows perfectly well how many other things are on his plate, and higher priority.  With his love of storytelling, he might even be done already.  So I'm guessing this won't slow them down appreciably.
